title: The Constitution of Kenya
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Facts: 18 chapters; Chapter 4 the Bill of Rights; Chapter 6 Leadership and Integrity; Chapter 8 the Legislature, 9 the Executive, 10 the Judiciary (to confirm). Three arms: Legislature makes laws, Executive carries them out, Judiciary interprets them.

skills.key_step: The child says what the Constitution contains, links the three arms to their work and chapters, and names principles of leadership and integrity.
steps: Name the chapters that matter here: 4 and 6.
Link each arm to its chapter.
contexts: a leader stepping aside over integrity

board.do: Write three principles: merit, honesty, accountability.

misconceptions.ask: Which arm interprets the law and settles disputes?
misconceptions.repair: Link each arm to one verb: make, carry out, interpret.

misconceptions.ask: Which chapter is the Bill of Rights?
misconceptions.repair: Look at the table of contents.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a principle of leadership and integrity?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a fair leader looks for.

misconceptions.ask: The President signs a bill into law. Which arm made the law?
misconceptions.repair: Trace a bill: debated and passed in Parliament, then signed.

checks.question: Which arm interprets the law and settles disputes?
Which chapter of the Constitution is the Bill of Rights?
